text: Oil volume matches the analytic value and is a single connected solid. Now the four patch surfaces, built explicitly rather than picked out of the boolean, so each name is fixed by construction.
Patch areas sum exactly to the oil boundary area, so the four sheets tile it with no overlap. Export one STL per patch.
Now the case skeleton and a coarse background mesh: 1 mm base cells, offset so the 1 mm gaps are not coincident with cell faces.
Mesh built. Now verify it against the geometry: volume, per-patch areas, and checkMesh.
Patch areas all within 0.7 % of CAD. Now a cut through the volume mesh to confirm the 1 mm gaps and the bore are actually resolved and connected.
Two cells across each 1 mm gap is marginal for a bearing clearance. Refine to level 2 (0.25 mm at the walls, ~4 cells per gap) and re-check.
Volume now matches CAD to 5 digits and the mesh is a single region (oil continuous through the gaps). Final patch areas and a cut view.
Let me check the welded union of the four STLs myself before declaring, since the ring wall and the end discs are separately tessellated.

The union welds shut with zero free edges (two bodies: the ring bore envelope and the spinner shell, as expected). Declaring complete.

**What I built.** The oil volume of the flooded bearing, in metres: everything inside the ring bore (r ≤ 23 mm, −5 ≤ z ≤ 5 mm) minus the spinner solid (r 15–22 mm, −4 ≤ z ≤ 4 mm). One connected solid — `checkMesh` reports **Number of regions: 1**, so the bore, the annular clearance and the two end gaps are a single region as required.

**Measured against the request:** radial clearance 1.000 mm, axial gap 1.000 mm at each end (both from the geometry, not assumed); CAD oil volume 10109.645 mm³ vs closed-form 10109.645 mm³; mesh total volume 1.01096e-5 m³ = 10109.6 mm³. Patch areas, mesh vs CAD: ringWall 1434.7/1445.1, spinnerWall 3463.7/3487.2, ringEndTop and ringEndBottom 1658.6/1661.9 mm² (0.2–0.7 % low, faceting on the curved walls).

**Patches**, each authored as its own surface and exported to `constant/triSurface/{name}.stl` before meshing: `ringWall` (the r = 23 mm bore), `spinnerWall` (the whole spinner surface: OD, bore, both ends), `ringEndTop`, `ringEndBottom`. Their areas sum exactly to the oil solid's area, so they tile the boundary with no overlap or gap.

**Mesh:** snappyHexMesh on a 1 mm background block (offset half a cell so the gap faces are not coincident with cell faces), level 2 at all walls → 0.25 mm, ~4 cells across each 1 mm gap; 291,831 cells, max non-orthogonality 42.0, max skewness 1.11, `Mesh OK`. No boundary layers added.

**My choices, not the request's:** (1) the request names "the ring's two annular end faces", but with the spinner ending 1 mm short of the ring the oil's caps at z = ±5 mm are *full discs* of radius 23 mm lying in the plane of the ring's annular ends — I exported them as those discs under `ringEndTop`/`ringEndBottom`; (2) the ring's 30 mm outer radius plays no part in the wetted volume and appears nowhere in the mesh; (3) all mesh resolution numbers (base 1 mm, level 2, no layers) are mine. **Not checked:** nothing about rotation, zones or solver setup — no cellZone or MRF region was created, and no fields exist.
The union fails winding: the end discs are almost certainly wound opposite to the ring wall at the two seam circles. Let me measure the orientation of each sheet.

`ringEndBottom` is wound with its normal into the oil while the other sheets face out — that is the seam mismatch. Fix the disc's orientation at construction and re-export all four, then re-verify the weld.
Now count the same thing the gate counts: directed edges walked twice the same way on the welded union.
Re-run the mesh from the corrected surfaces so the delivered mesh is the one built from the delivered STLs.

The winding warning was real and is fixed at its source: `ringEndBottom` was wound inward (its `Circle` face normal is +z while the envelope's outward there is −z). Reversing that face gives zero free edges and, on my own count of the welded union, zero directed edges traversed more than once. The mesh was then rebuilt from the corrected STLs and is identical: 291,831 cells, one region, total volume 1.01096e-5 m³, max non-orthogonality 42.0, max skewness 1.11, `Mesh OK`.

Everything else stands as reported above: clearances measured at 1.000 mm radial and 1.000 mm axial per end, patch areas within 0.7 % of CAD, four per-patch STLs in `constant/triSurface`. My assumptions remain (a) the oil caps at z = ±5 mm are full 23 mm discs coplanar with the ring's annular ends, exported as `ringEndTop`/`ringEndBottom`; (b) all resolution choices (1 mm base, level 2, no layers) are mine; (c) the 30 mm outer radius does not enter the wetted volume. Not checked: anything rotational — no cellZone, MRF or fields were created.
